openings.claim: Replace provisional point counts with certificates over unresolved flagged labels. Candidate-correct minus baseline-correct is zero for identical predictions; differing predictions have conservative [-1,1] bounds. Sum fixed/unresolved contributions overall/by slice. Advance only if total lower bound >=4 and every slice lower bound >=-2; reject if total upper bound <4 or any slice upper bound <-2; otherwise unresolved. This may support reproducibility and expose undecidable slices. Prioritize differing-prediction rows in slices whose bounds cross -2, then total-boundary rows; tie-break by supplied record ID.
openings.discriminator: Nearest rival: provisional confusion table then uniform flagged-row selection, using the same conservative reporting rule. Boundary priority may improve acceptance-relevant resolution; no directional gain assumed. Compare certificate widths, decisive reports, affected slices and successful adjudications at freeze. Unsupported decisive reports defeat certificate logic; equal resolution demonstrates no selection benefit.
openings.probe: Use supplied records/labels only and unchanged thresholds. Run both reproducible orders on matched copies with independent sixteen-successful-adjudication allowances and the same four preselected unavailable rows. Log selections, results, withheld attempts and time; attempts consume no allowance; exclude unavailable rows subsequently. Freeze both reports within seventy minutes before opening full-label decision key; compare decision agreement, unresolved frequency, boundary widths and logs.
openings.uncertainty: Declared fit uncertain. Only flagged labels assumed revisable under key; otherwise retain broader uncertainty. Seventy-minute implementation/audit capacity unconfirmed, preventing execution promises. Informative adjudication requires accessible differing-prediction rows affecting crossed boundaries; withholding/cap may leave unresolved bounds, requiring uncertainty. One matched trial offers limited evidence. Apparent gain and annotator disagreements motivate tracking without establishing update quality or deployment readiness.

decision: Retain R1 as an uncertain bounded evaluation probe; report advance, reject or unresolved only with supported certificates, never deployment readiness.
